content.user_title: Analyze Technical Debt and Plan Cleanup
content.value_statement: Technical debt slows delivery, raises defect rates, and makes modernization harder. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through measurable cleanup planning.
actual_capabilities: Identifies code, architecture, testing, documentation, and infrastructure debt categories.
Estimates cost, risk, and ROI for major debt items.
Creates measurable debt dashboards with quality and dependency metrics.
Builds prioritized cleanup roadmaps across quick wins and larger initiatives.
Defines quality gates to reduce new technical debt.
Produces stakeholder summaries for engineering and product planning.
limitations: Impact estimates depend on the codebase context and available engineering metrics.
It provides analysis and planning, not a guaranteed automated refactor.
It does not replace dedicated security, compliance, or performance audits.
Recommendations should be validated by code owners before scheduling major work.

use_cases.title: Plan Sprint Cleanup
use_cases.description: Identify quick wins and assign cleanup work with effort, savings, and delivery impact.

use_cases.title: Prepare Legacy Modernization
use_cases.description: Map architecture and dependency debt before a migration or framework upgrade.

use_cases.title: Justify Refactoring Investment
use_cases.description: Convert debt items into cost, risk, and ROI language for roadmap decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Find Top Debt Items
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this repository for the five highest-impact technical debt items. Include category, location, impact, and first remediation step.

prompt_templates.title: Create Cleanup Roadmap
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the codebase and create a 90-day technical debt roadmap. Prioritize quick wins, medium work, and long-term architecture improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Quantify Cost and ROI
prompt_templates.prompt: Estimate monthly engineering cost for each major debt item. Show assumptions, risk level, effort, savings, and expected payback period.

prompt_templates.title: Design Prevention System
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze current development workflow and propose automated quality gates, review standards, metrics, and ownership to prevent new debt.

output_examples.input: Audit an API service with duplicate validation and low integration coverage.
output_examples.output: Ranked debt inventory with duplicate validation as a quick win, payment flow tests as a high-risk gap, and a 30-day remediation plan.

output_examples.input: Prepare a modernization case for an outdated frontend framework.
output_examples.output: Business-facing summary with upgrade effort, risk reduction, dependency health, delivery impact, and staged migration milestones.

output_examples.input: Prevent recurring technical debt after a cleanup project.
output_examples.output: Quality gate plan covering complexity limits, coverage targets, dependency checks, code review rules, and quarterly debt reviews.

best_practices: Provide recent bug, deployment, and cycle-time data for more useful impact estimates.
Ask for debt to be ranked by user risk, delivery impact, and remediation effort.
Review recommendations with code owners before scheduling large refactors.
anti_patterns: Do not treat every style issue as technical debt without measurable impact.
Do not ask for broad rewrites before identifying quick wins and risk controls.
Do not use estimated ROI as a budget commitment without validating assumptions.

faq.question: Does this skill modify code?
faq.answer: It mainly creates analysis and plans. It can suggest changes, but users should request implementation separately.

faq.question: Can it run scanners?
faq.answer: It can recommend metrics and checks, but the skill itself does not include executable tooling.

faq.question: What inputs work best?
faq.answer: Provide repository context, recent incidents, test results, dependency status, and delivery pain points.

faq.question: Is it only for large repositories?
faq.answer: No. It can help small teams find focused cleanup work before debt becomes harder to manage.

faq.question: How should teams use the results?
faq.answer: Review the roadmap with code owners, confirm assumptions, and schedule the highest-impact work first.

faq.question: Does it replace security review?
faq.answer: No. It can identify security-related debt, but dedicated security review remains necessary for high-risk systems.
